concerns.location: plan.md:Learnability Classification – Relationship deemed learnable if R² > 0.0 and p < 0.05 from a global permutation test (1,000 shuffles) and RMSE < 150 mV
concerns.text: The plan uses a global permutation test on the R² statistic to assess learnability, then combines this p‑value with an RMSE threshold. While permutation testing of R² is acceptable, the subsequent RMSE cutoff is an arbitrary engineering rule (150 mV) not justified by statistical theory; it creates a hybrid decision rule that may misclassify models. Recommend either (a) define a statistically grounded confidence interval for RMSE via bootstrapping, or (b) rely solely on the permutation‑test p‑value for the learnability decision.

concerns.location: plan.md:Feature Importance – Permutation importance (1,000 permutations) with Bonferroni/FDR correction
concerns.text: Permutation importance assumes feature independence; however, compositional data (even after CLR transformation) remain linearly dependent (sum‑zero constraint) and often highly correlated. Applying permutation importance and standard multiple‑testing corrections can yield biased importance scores and inflated type‑I error. The plan should either (a) use a conditional permutation importance that accounts for feature correlation, or (b) adopt alternative importance measures (e.g., SHAP values) that are robust to correlated inputs.

concerns.location: plan.md:Partial Dependence – PDPs for top composition‑environment interactions
concerns.text: Partial dependence plots assume that the feature of interest can vary independently of other features. With compositional predictors that are constrained (sum‑to‑one) and correlated, PDPs can produce misleading marginal effects. The plan should either (a) employ accumulated local effects (ALE) plots, which are less sensitive to feature dependence, or (b) explicitly acknowledge and correct for the compositional constraint when interpreting PDPs.
